topics.title: Colombia inaugurates new president in Cali
topics.summary: Colombia's Abelardo de la Espriella is being sworn in under tight security in Cali, marking a rightward political shift and a tougher promised line on armed groups.
topics.discussionPrompt: If a new leader moved the big ceremony away from the capital to make a point, would you call that bold, theatrical, or both?

topics.title: Romania redirects the Danube for power
topics.summary: Romania is sinking rock-filled barges into the low Danube to steer water toward its Cernavoda nuclear plant and keep a second reactor running longer.
topics.discussionPrompt: When the river gets too low for a power plant, is sinking barges clever crisis engineering or the kind of plan that deserves a second coffee first?

topics.title: U.S. job market stalls in July
topics.summary: U.S. employers cut 23,000 jobs in July, a sharper-than-expected slowdown that put new attention on the economy and political arguments over jobs.
topics.discussionPrompt: When a jobs report suddenly changes the mood, do you think people trust the headline number or what they see in their own town?

topics.title: Kellogg to drop artificial cereal dyes
topics.summary: WK Kellogg says it will remove artificial colors from its cereals by the end of 2026, covering brands such as Froot Loops and Apple Jacks.
topics.discussionPrompt: If a bright cereal changes colors but tastes the same, would anyone at breakfast notice before reading the box?

topics.title: FDA approves mRNA flu shot
topics.summary: The FDA approved Moderna's mRNA-based flu vaccine for older adults, adding a new option ahead of future flu seasons.
topics.discussionPrompt: Would you be more curious about a new flu shot because it uses newer tech, or would that make you ask more questions first?
